scoring_justification: The paper's claims are captured by structural features of the three simulation outputs, not a single scalar metric. T1 recompute is infeasible because there is no single metric to recompute, and the outputs are not compared to a gold dataset. T2 consistency is not applicable. T3 structural audits of the spectrum, spatial extent, and time profile directly verify the key qualitative results described in the paper.

outputs.description: Differential energy spectrum of escaping secondary electrons. Checker verifies that the spectrum contains a data point with energy ≥ 30 MeV and non-zero flux.

Radial distribution of electron number per unit area at 500 km altitude. Checker verifies that the electron beam half-width at half-max is between 5 and 20 km, implying a factor ~10 narrower than the gamma-ray beam.

Simulated electron count rate vs time at satellite altitude, showing two distinct peaks separated by 5–15 ms with the second peak amplitude 0.5–2× the first. This artifact carries the highest weight and is load-bearing, requiring the full simulation chain.

output_contract.notes: All outputs are produced from the Monte Carlo and propagation pipeline. The checker performs structural audits: for energy_spectrum.csv it checks for presence of non-zero flux at >=30 MeV; for spatial_distribution.csv it computes the half-width at half-max and verifies it lies in 5–20 km; for time_profile.csv it identifies two distinct peaks with separation 5–15 ms and second-to-first amplitude ratio between 0.5 and 2.0. No gold numerical values are disclosed.
